subject: Title one schools
comment: Hi all After the last planning commission meeting I went to Teri McCabe, school board member, and asked her for some data. I found this school boundary map that I used to put information on. It is interactive in its original form in that if you click on the color it will give you the elementary school in which boundary it represents. Unfortunately I am not that tech savvy so you will have to zoom in to see the school names and % of disadvantaged on the attached map. https://www.zipdatamaps.com/schools/utah/district/map-of-provo-school-district-ut- elementary-school-attendance-zones Teri guided me to https://utahschoolgrades.schools.utah.gov Where I found every school’s data to place on the map. It is easier if you type in Provo in the pull down menu, this allows all Provo City School District schools to pop up in alphabetical order. From there you want to click on the 3 blue lines in the right corner…you will see home, performance and profile. You will want to click on profile to see the information. I hear council members tell me often that Provo has a large economically disadvantaged population because of the students. I have long said that is not the only reason; therefore I have provided the English learner percentage as well to show that Provo also has a significant amount of economical disadvantaged population that is NOT counted amongst the student population. I would like to point out that Spring Creek takes in most of the Franklin South neighborhood along with Spring Creek and Provost South Neighborhoods. I have been told that because of the conditions of Spring Creek MANY from Provost South as well as Spring Creek ELECT to attend Provost. I am sure the district can provide you with those numbers. With a school covering just one neighborhood, those kids to fill that school have to be coming from somewhere. From the numbers we see that the areas with the most disadvantaged populations fall in the Franklin and Franklin South Neighborhoods. This is followed by the Dixon, Timp, North Park and River Grove neighborhoods. With south west and south east Provo falling in a close third. All neighborhoods falling at nearly 60% or higher economically disadvantaged students. Where the conversation with the planning commission was focused on south east Provo, I would like the discussion to span everything south of Center street. I agree we need to build smart; however, we have a great need to balance out what is already here. So far in South West Provo I am seeing a big need for move up homes. Those will be provided with our 4 units to the acre. However, I would also like to point out that I am seeing people from all over Provo occupying these homes because move up homes is a product in our housing stock that is needed for not just south west Provo but the areas around us as well. Spring Creek … provost south, spring creek, Franklin south. 85% disadvantaged. 42% English Learner Franklin Franklin, 1/2 of Lakewood, some of down town. 81% disadvantaged 50% English Learner Timpanogas River grove, North Park, Dixon, Timp, a little of down town. 72% disadvantaged 49% English learner Amelia Earhart Fort Utah and Provo Bay 63% disadvantaged 26% English Learner. Provo Peaks Joaquin, part of Down Town, souther part of Foot Hills and Maesar 62% disadvantaged 30% English Learner Provost Provost Neighborhood 60% disadvantaged 24% English Learner Sunset Elementary Sunset, 1/2 Lakewood, and a tiny bit of Franklin South. 58% disadvantaged 29% English Learner -- Becky Bogdin Lakewood Neighborhood Chair
